Analysis complete. `analysis.py`, `result.json`, and `model_comparison.csv` are written.

## Finding (H1): Yes — but the effect is small among well-specified families

Nine model families, stratified 5-fold CV on all 48,790 de-duplicated rows, identical folds for every model (paired), out-of-fold ROC-AUC:

| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | Acc | F1(>50K) | LogLoss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **HistGradientBoosting** | **0.9289** | 0.829 | 0.873 | 0.712 | 0.276 |
| RandomForest (500) | 0.9181 | 0.809 | 0.867 | 0.691 | 0.296 |
| ExtraTrees (500) | 0.9119 | 0.785 | 0.859 | 0.664 | 0.314 |
| MLP (100,50) | 0.9114 | 0.779 | 0.856 | 0.673 | 0.311 |
| LogisticRegression | 0.9064 | 0.766 | 0.852 | 0.659 | 0.319 |
| DecisionTree (d=8) | 0.9050 | 0.776 | 0.855 | 0.645 | 0.321 |
| kNN (k=25) | 0.8642 | 0.661 | 0.837 | 0.644 | 0.869 |
| GaussianNB | 0.8294 | 0.532 | 0.617 | 0.536 | 6.62 |
| Baseline (prior) | 0.5000 | 0.239 | 0.761 | 0.000 | 0.550 |

**Headline:** HistGB − LogReg = **+0.0225 AUC** (95% paired-bootstrap CI +0.0211 to +0.0238; paired-fold t-test p ≈ 7e-7). The gain is tiny in absolute terms but utterly consistent — it held in all 5 folds with fold-wise SD of only 0.0009, and a holdout grid over LogReg's `C` and HGB's learning-rate/leaf-count reproduced the same +0.0227 gap, so it isn't a hyperparameter artefact.

Two things worth separating:

- **Among the six competently-specified families** (boosting, RF, ExtraTrees, MLP, logistic regression, single tree) the entire AUC range is **0.024** and the accuracy range 0.022. A single depth-8 decision tree is statistically indistinguishable from logistic regression (p = 0.11). This is a mostly-tabular, mostly-additive problem; the extra capacity buys little.
- **Mis-specification costs much more than family choice at the top.** Gaussian NB (−0.076 AUC, and badly uncalibrated at log loss 6.6 from its independence assumption over one-hot dummies) and kNN (−0.042, log loss 0.87) lose 2–3× more than boosting gains. Calibration diverges far more than ranking does.

The practical read: on Adult, model family *does* matter and boosted trees are the defensible default, but the deliverable difference is ~2 AUC points over a linear baseline — the choice matters mainly for avoiding a poor fit, not for large gains.

Two caveats on my choices that another researcher might make differently: I dropped `fnlwgt` (a census sampling weight, not a person-level attribute), and I used a random stratified 5-fold split rather than Adult's canonical 32,561/16,281 train/test split. I also gave tree models ordinal encoding with native categorical handling while linear/kNN/MLP/NB got one-hot — a shared encoding for all models would shift the tree numbers somewhat.

parsed_result.summary: Yes, but the size of the effect depends on which families you compare. Gradient-boosted trees are the best family (OOF ROC-AUC 0.9289) and beat logistic regression by +0.0225 AUC (95% CI +0.0211 to +0.0238, paired t p=6.8e-07) — a small but highly consistent gain. Across the six competently-specified families the whole AUC range is only 0.024, whereas mis-specified families (Gaussian NB, kNN) lose far more, so family choice matters mainly for avoiding bad fits rather than for large gains at the top.
parsed_result.direction: Gradient-boosted trees > RF/ExtraTrees/MLP > LogReg > single tree >> kNN/NaiveBayes; gap at the top is small (~0.02 AUC) but statistically robust
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Dropped 52 exact duplicate rows and the `fnlwgt` census sampling weight (not a person-level predictor); kept both `education` and `education-num` despite their redundancy. Missing values in workclass/occupation/native-country encoded as an explicit 'Missing' level rather than imputed, since missingness is informative. Two preprocessing paths: one-hot (min_frequency=10) + standardised numerics for LogReg/kNN/MLP/GaussianNB, ordinal codes with native categorical handling for the tree models — a researcher forcing one shared encoding on all models would shift the tree results slightly. Evaluation is 5-fold stratified CV over all 48,790 rows with identical folds for every model (paired), rather than the canonical Adult 32,561/16,281 train/test split. Primary metric ROC-AUC because the classes are imbalanced (24% positive) and it is threshold-free; accuracy, PR-AUC, F1@0.5 and log loss reported alongside. No class-imbalance correction (no class_weight, no resampling) — the goal is ranking quality, not a calibrated decision rule. Hyperparameters were fixed a priori at sensible defaults rather than tuned per model, so this answers 'out-of-the-box family performance'; a separate 75/25 holdout grid over LogReg C and HGB learning-rate/leaf-count confirms tuning does not reverse the ranking. Significance from a paired t-test over 5 fold-wise AUCs (only 5 pairs, so treated as indicative) plus a 1000-replicate paired row bootstrap on the pooled out-of-fold predictions for the headline contrast.
